instructions: Class assignment 2 (Modules 4 to 6), set by the Big Data Analytics faculty.
Marks are not printed on the assignment; each answer is written at the length of a 10-mark exam answer, and short definitions at 5 marks.

questions.text: What is sampling in a data stream? Explain any two sampling techniques used for stream data.
State the constraints used for bucket creation in the DGIM algorithm.

Consider a Bloom Filter of size 10 bits, initially set to 0. Three hash functions are defined as: h1(x) = x mod 10, h2(x) = (2x+1) mod 10, h3(x) = (3x+2) mod 10. (i) Insert the elements 8, 5, and 13 into the Bloom Filter. (ii) Then determine whether the element 9 is possibly present in the set or definitely absent. Show all intermediate steps and the final Bloom Filter bit array.

Consider the following stream: 1,2,5,4,3,2,2,8. Apply the Flajolet-Martin algorithm to estimate the number of distinct elements in the given data stream. Use the hash function h(x) = (3x+1) mod 32. Show the hash values, their 5-bit binary representations, number of trailing zeros, maximum trailing zeros R, and the final estimated number of distinct elements using D = 2^R.
Explain the CURE (Clustering Using REpresentatives) algorithm and describe how representative points are used to form clusters.
Explain the concept of Distance Measure and write different types of it.
Analyze and justify the use of a Content-Based Recommendation System with a suitable real-world case study.
Explain how a classification algorithm can be applied in a recommendation system to predict whether a user will like or dislike a particular item. Illustrate with a suitable example.
What is PageRank? State its main purpose in analyzing web pages.
